speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry in respect of the study to understand nuclear technology, safety of nuclear power plant technologies and their viability for Singapore (a) whether the study will include (i) an estimate timeframe for deployment of nuclear energy and (ii) potential sites for the reactors, where it is found to be viable for Singapore; and (b) whether the key risks identified in the study will be published.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry on the Government’s recent setup of dedicated nuclear teams at the Energy Market Authority and the National Environment Agency (a) what is the readiness to deploy nuclear energy in Singapore; and (b) what is the staff strength of the nuclear team at these two respective agencies.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry regarding the dedicated nuclear teams set up at the Energy Market Authority and the National Environment Agency, whether the Government will consider including representatives from other sectors and the public in these teams to address common concerns, such as safety and perceptions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are studying the potential for nuclear energy deployment as it is a low-carbon energy source that enhances our energy security.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As part of our overall efforts to build capabilities to assess whether the latest nuclear technologies could be suitable for deployment in Singapore, we have set up dedicated nuclear energy teams in the Energy Market Authority (EMA) and the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The EMA and NEA teams are made up of Public Service officers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They will be adequately resourced to carry out their roles and will be collaborating with partners from other governments, as well as with industry and academia.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared right at the beginning, because we have not made any decision on deploying nuclear energy in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will engage the public regularly on the latest developments in nuclear energy to build an informed understanding on nuclear energy.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Many people are quite concerned about the health and also the safety impact of nuclear energy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have said earlier on, we have not made the decision on whether to deploy nuclear energy technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, in the run-up, we have got the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute (SNRSI); we have just upgraded it to an institute.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the same time, given the fact that we have just published the background paper to showcase what our journey has been thus far, we will continuously work with different governments and different jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And as the updated safety profiles of this advanced nuclear technology come on, we will share them with the public to build background knowledge and also to socialise our larger population.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Even if we eventually decide that we will not go down the pathway of deploying on our shores, it does not preclude our neighbouring countries from deploying on their shores.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And that education would involve getting big parts of our population to be socialised to the idea that our neighbours may also deploy that, and what are the safety considerations and measures that we should be undertaking.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives the Member that reassurance.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: If Singapore were to build a nuclear reactor for the purpose of power generation, whether it would be located in the far part of Singapore or on the offshore islands.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: A second supplementary question is, if we were to decide to build a nuclear plant, what is the timeframe?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Does it take 10 or 15 years to build?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, the Member missed the earlier part of the answer.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have not decided whether to deploy nuclear energy technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I think it is premature for us, given the fact that we have not decided, to talk about potential deployment sites and also whether it is going to be on an offshore island, in the sea or underground.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The journey over the next few years will allow us to understand many of these advanced nuclear energy technologies, the promise they hold and while the current thinking is the physics, the engineering works, the commercial feasibility and the viability has still yet to be proven.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, as result, the study is quite focused on comparing the different types of advanced nuclear technology and whether the safety profile, whether the type of outputs that they generate, how efficient they are, will eventually benefit us or not.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, as far as the timeline is concerned, we have not even made the decision.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think the timeline is even further out.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I cannot comment in a very definitive manner as to what kind of timelines we are looking at.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What I can safely say is from the results of the 2012 study that we have completed, and if the Member could look back at the report that was released, is that conventional nuclear power and nuclear energy technology, the conventional ones, those that involve very large conventional reactors is not suitable for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And hence, we have no plans to even look at deploying those.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives the Member that clarity that he needs.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Public engagement is a strategic activity for building trust, understanding and the concerns of the community, and ensuring that local needs and preferences are considered in nuclear project planning.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My supplementary question is, could the Ministry elaborate more on plans to enhance public literacy on nuclear technologies, especially among youths and non-technical communities, so that future discussions are informed and inclusive?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Given that in Singapore, we have a very densely populated, very urbanised environment, we want to also not alarm the public.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We want to continually engage them regularly on the latest developments in nuclear energy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have said earlier on, even if we ultimately decide not to deploy here, it does not mean our neighbours will not deploy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, as the regional interest in nuclear powers continues to grow, we want to contemporaneously and progressively prepare our fellow Singaporeans for the potential deployment of nuclear energy in the region.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: After all, we have a very small footprint.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Like what they always say in Mandarin, "我们是弹丸小国".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And what are the mitigating actions that could be taken in the unlikely event of an accident in nuclear energy facilities in the region?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That is what we will proceed with on very sure-footed steps.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that gives you the reassurance that you need, Dr Choo.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The ones that he alluded to, the molten salt reactor, light-water, including thorium, we also need to consider the supply chain.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, given our understanding of the supply chain for thorium, the concentration risk in terms of the procurement of the supply of thorium is actually quite limited.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And when we get the results of that study some time down the line, we will be able to make a more meaningful comparison.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I am sure by that time, Parliamentary Questions will be filed, and I am happy to update the House again.
